title: What If the Moon Disappeared?
lines: What if the Moon suddenly disappeared?
Without it, | moonlit nights would be {about 100~about a hundred} times darker.
Then the tides. | The Moon does most of the pulling.
With only the Sun left, | tides would shrink to about a third of today's biggest.
And total solar {eclipses/~eclipses} would be gone, forever.
The Moon also steadies Earth's tilt.
Without it, | many models say that {tilt/~tilt} could wobble far {more,/~more,} and seasons could go haywire.
But here's the twist: | the Moon is already slowly leaving us.
Every year, | it drifts about {3.8 centimeters~three point eight centimeters} farther away.
That's about as fast as your fingernails grow.
How long until total solar eclipses end? | {About 6,000 years~About six thousand years}, or {about 600 million years~about six hundred million years}? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: The Moon is already leaving us.
